title: World Foundation announced Phase 3 utility-first growth and reported over 900m WLD distributed
description: In its June 9, 2026 Simple Plan, World Foundation announced Phase 3, moving growth emphasis from token incentives toward Proof-of-Human product utility. It reported approximately 16 million WLD recipients and over 900 million WLD granted as user grants/referrals, together with over 18 million human proofs and over 450 million World ID uses. These are issuer-reported aggregate figures, not audited user uniqueness, wallet settlement, or independent token-distribution verification.
notes: Source sections 'Phase 2: Launch and bootstrap the network through token ownership', 'Phase 3', and 'Shift to utility-based growth'. Preserve distinction between verified humans, eligible WLD claimants, unique token recipients and usage counts; definitions may differ. No current WLD wallet or purchaser inference.

title: World Foundation planned five-country operational concentration and 95% self-service Orbs by 2026 end
description: On June 9, 2026, World Foundation described a shift toward concentrated Proof-of-Human deployment in the United States (San Francisco and New York), United Kingdom, Germany, Japan, and South Korea; it projected 95% of Orbs would be self-service by the end of 2026. The source also anticipated reducing the physical operations footprint outside focus countries and workforce impacts. These are prospective plans rather than verified deployment counts, closures, or layoffs.
notes: Source section 'Refining the operational footprint around utility and density'. U.S. city examples are within the U.S. focus country, not additional countries. The 95% Orb metric is a stated end-2026 target; no October 2026 measured percentage was verified.

title: World Foundation proposed application-paid World ID fees and future decentralization
description: The June 9, 2026 strategy states that World ID 4.0 enables an anticipated fee model paid by applications, with protocol usage intended to remain free to end users, and identifies enterprise identity security as the near-term opportunity. It places further governance/infrastructure decentralization in future Phase 4 rather than documenting completion in Phase 3. World separately describes the Foundation as initial protocol steward and TFH as a separate service provider.
notes: Source 'World ID fees and protocol revenue' and 'Phase 4: Scale further through utility and decentralize'; World About FAQ 'Who owns World?' and 'What is Tools for Humanity?'. Do not infer actually booked protocol revenue, production fees, active governance keys, or Foundation legal ownership by TFH from this plan. World says Zoom integration via the ISV platform expected in the next six months, not completed at the date of this announcement.

locators: World ID fees and protocol revenue
Phase 4: Scale further through utility and decentralize
